hana: Build failed: linkcheck flagged missing fragment on /cookbook/parsing#parsing-code-block-headings. The source has a code fence immediately before the heading, e.g.:

```md
```python
# example
```
## Parsing code-block headings

But the produced HTML id becomes `parsing-code-block-headings-1` and our old site had `parsing-code-block-headings`. Any ideas?

vic: Interesting. Code fences shouldn't affect heading ids, but if there's an unclosed fence or an HTML comment before the heading the parser can behave differently. Also some markdown processors treat the fence+heading as part of the same block, altering slug output.

omar: Repro locally quickly:
```bash
cat docs/cookbook/parsing.md | sed -n '1,120p'
# then run our two slug tools
node ./scripts/docusaurus-slugify.js "$(node ./scripts/extract-heading.js docs/cookbook/parsing.md 'Parsing code-block headings')"
node ./scripts/legacy-slugify.js "$(node ./scripts/extract-heading.js docs/cookbook/parsing.md 'Parsing code-block headings')"
```
I see docusaurus -> "parsing-code-block-headings" and legacy -> "parsing-code-block-headings" for the clean file, but on the migrated file legacy produced `parsing-code-block-headings` and the built HTML ended up with a `-1` suffix because an empty heading id was emitted earlier (a phantom id from an unclosed fence).

hana: Where did the phantom id come from?

vic: In a few migrated files we left behind stray triple-backticks without a language tag or the closing fence due to conversion errors. The markdown parser then autogenerates a placeholder node that can grab an id. Also some editors add invisible ZWNBSP right after a fence which confuses the parser.

omar: Quick fixes I can push: 1) a lint that fails if there are unmatched code fences (counts of ``` not even), 2) a normalize step that removes stray ZW chars around fences, 3) a migration clean-up that closes open fences or converts them into proper fenced blocks.

hana: Sounds good. Also we should add a targeted linkcheck test that runs after the migration pass to catch `-1` suffixes for anchors referenced in the inbound-links export. If we detect a `-1` we should try to find a matching anchor without suffix and auto-create a redirect.

vic: For safety, make the redirect generator conservative: only add redirects when the unsuffixed anchor exists in the analytics inbound list or when the content is unchanged except for the id suffix. Otherwise manual review.

omar: I'll open a small PR with: - docs-lint rule `fence-closed` - normalize-fences.js to strip U+00AD/U+200B/U+200C around fences - generate-redirects-for-suffixed-ids.js (with inbound-links filter) - unit tests for an unclosed fence scenario

docs-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5901 by omar  add fence hygiene + redirect helper + lint

hana: Nice. One more edge case: admonitions (::: note) followed immediately by an H3 sometimes produce different anchor rules. Let's add a test for `::: note
### Tip heading` vs `### Tip heading` to the slug-compare matrix.

vic: Good catch. I'll add that test vector.

linkcheck-bot: Docs CI (linkcheck) reported 2 missing fragments. Re-run after PR merge.

hana: Thanks all 1: once merged we'll re-run full linkcheck across migrated cookbooks and the inbound-least-popular list to avoid spam redirects.
